prompt: The table shows how $200$ students commute to school. If one student is selected at random, what is the probability that the student walks? Give your answer as a decimal.
hint: A probability compares the outcomes you want with all possible outcomes. Decide which two numbers in the table those are.

hints.text: A probability compares the outcomes you want with all possible outcomes. Decide which two numbers in the table those are.
No grade is specified, so the whole group of $200$ students is the denominator. The Walk row has a total of $50$ students. Divide.
The fraction $\dfrac{50}{200}$ equals $0.25$, so the probability is $0.25$.

learningObjective: Read a simple probability from a two-way table.
explanation: The question puts no condition on grade, so every one of the $200$ students could be chosen.
The Walk row of the table has a total of $50$ students, and these are the favorable outcomes.
Divide favorable by total: $\dfrac{50}{200} = 0.25$, so the probability is $0.25$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Find the denominator before the numerator
steps: "Selected at random" from all students means the grand total, $200$.
Had the question said "selected from Grade 9", the denominator would be $110$ instead.
Circling the denominator in the table first is the habit that makes every two-way-table question routine.
